stories.title: Application study of a water conducting fracture zone height prediction model based on bp neural network optimized by genetic algorithme
stories.description: It is important to accurately predict the height of the water conducting fracture zone (WCFZ) for the production safety of coal mines and ecological environmental protection. Through the field measurement data of WCFZ at working face in Shendong and neighboring mines. The correlation degree between the working face length, mining height, mining depth, coal seam dip angle, mining speed, hard rock proportionality coefficient and the height of WCFZ was analyzed by using gray relationship analysis theory. The BP neural network model optimized by genetic algorithm was trained, and the predicted WCFZ values of empirical formula, GA-BP and BP neural network model were compared with the actual measured values of WCFZ in the mine area. The comparison analysis showed that the GA-BP neural network model had the smallest error of 7.78% in the prediction value. Therefore, the GA-BP neural network model has sufficient prediction accuracy and generalizability and can be applied to study the WCFZ in the Shendong mine area.

stories.title: A fuzzy c-means based dual-layer flux-blending framework for high-resolution dam-break simulations
stories.description: Dam-break flow modelling involves a trade-off as resolving steep gradients requires high-order discretisations, yet these tend to generate spurious oscillations near discontinuities. Moreover, classical limiters used to suppress such oscillations rely largely on single-parameter algebraic indicator rules. This study replaces the procedure with a fuzzy c-means flux-blending framework for the finite-volume solution of the shallow water equations. To this end, an unsupervised classifier is trained on local hydraulic descriptors to assign each interface a shock-membership grade, and a second fuzzy inference layer converts that grade into a weight that blends a high-order flux with a dissipative low-order flux. The limiter-based transition is thereby replaced by a data-driven transition whose behaviour is determined by a measurable flow structure rather than a fixed algebraic rule. Accordingly, dissipation is graded continuously with the local flow structure. To validate the framework, one- and two-dimensional wet-bed and dry-bed dam-break benchmarks, including circular and partial-breach configurations, are considered. Against the exact Stoker and Ritter solutions, the scheme attains $$\:{L}_{1,h}$$ errors of 0.0664 and 0.0257 for the one-dimensional wet-bed and dry-bed cases, respectively, placing it between the first-order Rusanov scheme and the Minmod-TVD limiter. In the two-dimensional partial breach, the framework produces a qualitatively similar diffraction pattern to the Minmod-TVD scheme without inducing non-physical oscillations. For the configurations tested, graded and interpretable flux control provides a viable alternative to limiter-based transition.

stories.title: Structural lightweight design of bogie bolster based on surrogate models
stories.description: The bogie bolster is one of the key components of railway freight cars, and its lightweight design plays an important role in improving the transportation capacity of freight vehicles. However, the bolster features complex geometry, leading to high costs and long design cycles in structural development. In this paper, finite element analysis (FEA) is performed to evaluate the static strength and stiffness of the bolster. An optimization model is established taking the geometric dimensions of process holes as design variables, the minimum mass of the bolster as objective function, and allowable stress and deformation as constraint conditions. The Kriging surrogate model is constructed for mass, stress and deformation responses. Then expected improvement (EI) criterion is adopted for sample infilling to improve model prediction performance, and genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to solve the optimization problem. Global Sobol sensitivity analysis is further implemented to quantify the contribution of each design variable to structural responses. After obtaining the lightweight scheme, finite-element-based fatigue simulation and modal characteristic analysis are carried out for post-verification to assess the service reliability of the optimized bolster. Numerical results show that the optimized structure satisfies the static-strength and stiffness constraints in the optimization formulation. Post-verification demonstrates that the optimized structure also meets fatigue and modal-performance specifications. The total mass of the bogie bolster is reduced by 16.20 kg, achieving the lightweight target for heavy-duty freight bogie bolsters.

stories.title: Specific macronutrient clusters associated with biological aging
stories.description: Nutrition is a key modifiable factor influencing aging, yet most studies focus on isolated nutrients or predefined dietary patterns, leaving the relationship between naturally occurring macronutrient clusters and biological aging poorly understood. This study aimed to identify naturally occurring macronutrient intake clusters using a novel three-dimensional approach and examine their associations with biological aging in U.S. adults. Data from 25,987 adults in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) were analyzed. Biological age was estimated using the Klemera-Doubal method (KDM-BA). Biological age acceleration (AA) was computed as the difference between biological age and chronological age. Dietary intake was assessed using 24-hour recalls. Participants were classified into macronutrient clusters based on energy percentages from protein, fat, and carbohydrates using percentile-based cutoffs. Multivariable weighted logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations between macronutrient clusters and AA, with stratification by energy intake, sex, and age. Compared to the reference cluster (Pm: Fm: Cmh—moderate protein, moderate fat, moderate-high carbohydrate), the Pm: Fm: Cm cluster (moderate protein, moderate fat, moderate carbohydrate) (OR: 1.21, 95% CI: 1.06–1.38) and the Pm: Fmh: Cml cluster (moderate protein, moderate-high fat, moderate-low carbohydrate) (OR: 1.25, 95% CI: 1.03–1.50) showed suggestive positive associations with AA. However, after adjusting for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) method, neither cluster reached the prespecified level of statistical significance (FDR q = 0.063 and 0.086, respectively). These associations were more pronounced in females and middle-aged adults (40–60 years). In restricted cubic spline analyses, a U-shaped relationship was observed for carbohydrate intake within Cluster Pl: Fm: Cml: AA risk decreased as carbohydrate intake increased from low to moderate levels, then increased with further higher carbohydrate intake (P overall = 0.031; P non-linear = 0.050). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential effect modification by demographic factors, but these findings should be interpreted with caution due to limited statistical power. Specific, naturally occurring macronutrient clusters showed suggestive associations with AA, with potential effect heterogeneity by energy intake, sex, and age. Our findings underscore the importance of moving beyond isolated nutrients toward a holistic dietary pattern approach and suggest preliminary avenues for personalized nutritional interventions. These associations warrant validation in future prospective studies.
